question: how do i find out why my financial aid hasnt shown up yet and who do i talk to

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status. Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

To check your account, click “here” for details, then click “Billing and Financial Aid Terminology.” [1] On the Account Summary screen, Pending Financial Aid is estimated or anticipated aid; Authorized Aid has met payment requirements and is credited on the official term disbursement date, typically four weeks into a term. [32] Memos need further action unless they are a New Jersey Class Loan, Alternative Loan, or Outside Scholarship; those are credited when payment is received from the funding agency. [32] For other Memos, the page strongly recommends contacting Financial Aid to resolve outstanding issues. [32]

I don’t have verified information about why aid hasn’t appeared in your individual account. [32] Contact the Office of Financial Aid. Appointments can be arranged by email or through the chat on its website; most questions can also be handled by phone, Webex, or email. [9]

- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [33]

question: refund

body.answer:
For student-account credit balance refunds, contact Student Accounts. A Title IV financial aid overpayment resulting in a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; credit balances from non-Title IV financial aid have a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks cannot be sent to campus mailboxes or picked up at Student Accounts. If entitled to a fall-term refund, you may ask Student Accounts by email at studentaccts@ramapo.edu to apply it to spring. Spring refunds cannot be applied to the following fall. [1]

To set up free direct deposit, log into RCNJ Experience; locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite; click Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup. Enroll in Two-Step Verification if needed: in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method, click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify. Then click Payment Profile and edit or create a payment method; check the box in Refund Option to designate it for direct deposit. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

After the published withdrawal deadline, a student may not withdraw through the standard course-withdrawal process [12]. For extraordinary circumstances that prevented withdrawal through standard procedures for reasons beyond the student’s control, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit to the Office of the Provost, no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term, an appeal letter in your own words supported by official documentation. Explain the extraordinary circumstances, why standard withdrawal or incompletes were unavailable, and the term requested; typically, approval results in W grades for all courses in that term [13].

Withdrawing may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation [8]. If you officially withdraw or leave school before 60% of a semester concludes, federal regulations determine the Title IV aid retained and returned; Financial Aid strongly recommends discussing a possible class withdrawal with its office [1]. Aid can change if dropping below full-time: federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled for 6 or more credits, while NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when fully disbursed [28]. SAP is reviewed annually after spring; students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits, and the page also sets GPA and maximum-time-frame standards [2].

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [34]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Orientation Programs’ parking-permit instructions: Apply online at the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). Log on; enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number. It verifies your application but is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status and “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [1] Parking fees are charged to your student account. Students living off campus are also charged 6.63% NJ sales tax; students living on campus are exempt. [1][19]
Commuters receive a rearview-mirror hangtag; two vehicles may be registered on one permit at no additional fee, but only one registered vehicle may be on campus at a time. [1][4] New students pick up permits during New Student Check-In. Returning commuters pick them up at the Public Safety ID Office Monday–Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pickup time. [1][4]
Public Safety: Commuters may park in B1, B2, or B3. If your assigned lot is full, students may use C1, C2, or D as overflow. Commuters may not leave vehicles overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [8]
The newer instructions use the RCNJ Parking Permits website; an older “How do I purchase a parking permit?” page (July 2022) describes a different ThePermitStore.com process. [1][2]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [19](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm a commuter student and I have a 3 hour gap between classes. Is there somewhere on campus I can study or hang out, like a commuter lounge, and is there a way to store my stuff?

body.answer:
The Center for Student Involvement says J. Lee’s is the unofficial Commuter Lounge, where students can relax; it has video games, pool and ping-pong tables, and free popcorn. It’s on the second floor of the Student Center, between the Student Government and Black Student Union offices. [1] Commuters can also hang out at J. Lee’s for games and free popcorn. [2] The Atrium in the Robert A. Scott Student Center has ample lounging areas. [20] The Women’s Center & LGBTQ+ Services welcomes students to use its lounge in Room C-220 to socialize or study during open hours; it has comfortable seating, a coffee maker, refrigerator and microwave. [14]

For storage, the Center for Student Involvement says students may rent small or medium lockers at the Student Center Office for $10.00 per semester or $20.00 per academic year. Lockers are in the second-floor stairwell between B and C buildings. You receive a key with payment and must return it at the end of the semester. [6]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/involvement-frequently-asked-questions/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/commuter-affairs/commuter-resources/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/womenscenter/about-the-center/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/tours/dining-shopping/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. The policy permits each registered guest to stay no more than three nights (consecutively or not) in a seven-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. Residents can host up to two guests at a time. Guests must remain with their host, carry valid ID, and have access to their approved Guest Registration email if on campus after 10:00 PM. Current Ramapo residential students do not need guest registration. [3]

You can opt out of the automatic assumption that roommates agree to guest registration by contacting your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. If the contract is violated, hall/area office staff need a formal complaint before acting; a complaint may mean all residents lose guest privileges until a contract is developed. The policy recommends discussing guest expectations with your roommate. [3]

Contact Housing & Residence Life or your Resident Assistant. Alleged violations of the Guide to Community Living should be filed with the Office of Residence Life. [3][16]

Overnight guests are not permitted on campus after Monday, December 14, 2026; residents with an approved check-out extension may not have guests. [6]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/student-complaints-of-a-non-academic-nature/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
All students parking on campus need a current, valid permit. [1]

The Orientation Programs FAQ says permits are online only through the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). [1] Public Safety says to ensure the parking fee has been applied to your student account, then visit that page. [4]

To apply: [1]
1. “Log on directly to the RCNJ Parking Permits website.”
2. “Enter Permit Type and click Continue.”
3. “Complete the Contact Information page, and then click Save/Update Person and then click Continue.”
4. “Enter Vehicle Information and then click Continue.”
5. “Review your request and then click Continue.”
6. “Print or save the Registration Filed page, which includes your registration request number.” This confirms your application; it is not the permit.

Choose “student,” not “faculty/staff,” and the correct housing or commuter status. New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning resident students at their on-campus mailbox; returning commuter students at the Public Safety ID Office during weekday operating hours. After 3 pm, commuters may request another pickup time by emailing parkingpermits@ramapo.edu. [1] Commuters may register two vehicles on one permit at no extra fee, but only one registered vehicle may be parked on campus at a time. [1][4]

 Off-campus students are subject to 7% sales tax; on-campus students are exempt. [5] An older Student Accounts page (June 2026) says 6.63%, and its older fee list (July 2026) gives a $16.58 Fall/Spring commuter tax charge. [9][16]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
That's a big decision, and it's worth talking it through with someone before you decide.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline. If your course is still within its withdrawal period, use Web Self Service; if you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email with your name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. After withdrawing from all courses, complete the WD/LOA process in Connect. [6]

Once processed, a course withdrawal is recorded as a W on your transcript, and you and the instructor of record are notified. There is no refund after the refund period ends. [1][6] The College encourages you to discuss withdrawal with your professor; withdrawal may affect financial aid, progress toward graduation, housing, athletics, or campus activities. [1]

For extraordinary circumstances beyond your control, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal: submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. A granted appeal typically results in W grades for all courses in the term. [7]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]

These offices can help:
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [23]
- **Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [23]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

**Facilities Management**

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Offices: P-FAC [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

Offices: C-102 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

This office can help:
**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
The Guide to Community Living lists candles as prohibited; students who do not comply may face disciplinary action [14]. Published sanctions specifically address activating a fire alarm by disregarding policy (candles and incense are examples): 1st offense—$150 fine and a fire safety reflection assignment; 2nd offense—$300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges [2]. Those sanctions do not establish what applies to your write-up if no fire alarm was activated or what your prior record is.

The pages don’t say whether an RA write-up automatically requires a hearing or whether your case will have one. The hearing page says the meeting is an opportunity to discuss what happened; it advises against trying to avoid responsibility, which usually results in more severe sanctions [7]. You may ask to review statements and incident reports by arranging an appointment or requesting the file from the Office of Student Conduct. You may bring an advisor, who may not speak during the hearing [1]. Contact the Office of Student Conduct to ask whether a hearing is required in your case.

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/frequently-asked-questions/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says a Title IV financial aid overpayment resulting in a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; credit balances from non-Title IV aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address. Checks cannot be mailed to campus mailboxes or picked up at Student Accounts. [1]

Direct deposit is optional and free. To enroll, follow these steps: [1][2]
1. Log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/).
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click on Bill & Payment Suite.
3. Click on Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu.
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a method to receive a passcode (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify.
5. Click Payment Profile in My Profile. Edit an existing payment method or create a new one, then check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it as the refund account. [3]

Eligible refunds are expected to be deposited within one to two weeks of submitting the application. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts says authorized users can make payments on your behalf. To add your parent: [4]
1. Log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/).
2. Locate the Student Account Info card.
3. Click on Bill & Payment Suite link.
4. Click on Authorized Users located on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section.
5. Click on the Add Authorized User tab.
6. Enter the email address of the desired authorized user, answer questions, and click the Continue button.
7. Click I Agree box then the Continue button.

To let them pay without seeing your bill or payment history, select ‘No’ for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history” when adding them. [3] The authorized user will be emailed a link and login credentials for the Bill and Payment Suite. [3]

Authorized users do not get access to your academic records or other personal information, and adding them does not authorize Student Accounts to discuss your financial records with them. To permit that discussion, complete and submit the Registrar’s Office FERPA Waiver form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open](https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open). [1][6]

question: how do i set up my campus email and wifi login

body.answer:
**Email — IT Help Desk:** Visit [https://password.ramapo.edu/](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” You can set up your account within 24 hours of receiving your Ramapo ID number. A valid Ramapo email account is required to register for classes. [8] MFA is required for Ramapo Gmail. When you sign in on a new device, verify your identity via the Gmail app; approve the prompt. Trust only devices you own, never public or shared computers. [4][2]

**Wi-Fi — ResNET:** To connect to ResNET, you need a valid Ramapo email account and a device capable of wireless or wired network connectivity. [6] Register the device you want to use with ResNET before it connects; once registered, it can be used campus-wide. [3] First determine whether you’ll use wired or wireless, then retrieve the MAC address of that connection; instructions for finding it are at [https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/). [15] Register at [https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/) and choose wired or wireless. [14] For wireless, scan for networks and connect; the page links to wireless instructions. [17] If you’re using an iPad, select “Ramapo-Secure” in Settings > Wi-Fi, enter your Ramapo username and password, then click Accept on the certificate warning. [10]

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Contact Housing & Residence Life. Review the [Room Change Process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) and the [Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/) before submitting a request; the calendar explains how a room change might affect you. [1] Once housing assignments have been made, room changes cannot be accommodated before the semester starts. Submit the Room Change Request Form during the open room change period. [2] The [online form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog) is available during active room change periods. [1][5] Requests are not guaranteed; they depend on available space and other factors, and professional Residence Life staff make the final decision. [1] Residence Life reserves the right to reassign students for unresolved conflict, among other reasons. [4] If approved, prorated housing charges and any applicable meal-plan changes will be assessed and adjusted on your student account. Housing costs vary by building, area, and housing-unit type; review costs on the [Student Accounts website](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts). [2] If you have a current parking permit, return your old permit at the Office of Public Safety (ID room) to receive a new one, and update your parking information if applicable. Questions: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu. [3] All room and board changes must be done through Residence Life. [7]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says all on-campus jobs are posted on Handshake. Register there, search “RCNJ,” follow the instructions on each posting, and apply to the hiring unit; contact the supervisor listed. Students awarded Federal Work-Study as part of their aid package receive priority for Student Assistant positions. [5] The hiring supervisor describes the job and decides whether to offer you the position. [1]

If you’re offered a job and accept it, you and the supervisor sign an employment form. Return the required new-hire packet, W-4 Form, and I-9 Form to the Student Assistant Program Office, Room D-119. [1]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [21]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts offers four- and five-month plans for Spring 2027, beginning November 16, 2026. Enroll online by logging into RCNJ Experience before the semester’s posted payment deadline. At enrollment, pay the down payment—25% for the four-month plan or 20% for the five-month plan—plus the non-refundable $60 set-up fee. Additional payments are due on the 15th of each month thereafter. Past-due balances of $500 or greater from previous semesters must be paid before you are eligible to enroll; the College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
For the 2027–2028 FAFSA, returning students should apply by April 1, and new students no later than May 1. The FAFSA is available at [https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa); Ramapo’s School Code is 009344. [14][1] Returning students who received an NJ TAG Grant must also complete the FAFSA by April 1. [15] An older Financial Aid FAFSA page, updated July 2025, gives March 15 for new students instead. [12]

For students generally, the pages don’t specify additional documents beyond completing required forms on time. [3] If you’re an EOF applicant, you must submit the FAFSA listing Ramapo (or, if qualified as a NJ undocumented student, the NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application), activate your NJFAMS account, and may need additional documents based on your status. [7] For EOF freshmen, FAFSA materials include parent tax forms if claimed as a dependent, student tax forms, untaxed-income records, investment records, bank statements, and W-2 forms. [29]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/admissions/financial-aid-tuition/financial-aid-deadlines/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/admissions/financial-aid-tuition/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/educational-opportunity-fund/admission-requirements/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/fafsa/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/calendar/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/financial/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline. After the refund period, a course withdrawal records a “W” on your transcript and gives no refund; the page says instructor permission is not required. [12] The Fall 2026 deadline for full-semester courses was November 6, 2026, already passed; Session II's deadline is November 24, 2026. [21]

For exceptional circumstances beyond your control, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the circumstances, why standard withdrawal/incomplete procedures were not possible, and the term you want withdrawn. [13] The Registrar page also says the letter should explain why you did not apply before semester-end, if applicable. [13]

Withdrawing may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation, among other things. [8] Financial Aid says students who officially withdraw or leave school before 60% of a semester concludes are subject to federal rules determining how much Title IV aid they may retain or must return. It recommends meeting with Financial Aid to discuss impacts of withdrawing from any classes. [1] Financial Aid SAP requires completing at least 67% of credits attempted; undergraduates need a cumulative 2.0 GPA and graduate students 3.0 at annual review. [2]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is my 1098-T available yet? need it for taxes and cant find where to get it. also how do i get a copy of last years

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

Student Accounts says it cannot confirm whether your individual form is available. Eligible students’ forms are provided on or before January 31 each year; the form is based on the prior tax year, and eligibility requires qualified tuition and related expenses and corresponding payments during the tax year. [2]

To check and download a copy for the appropriate tax year, use the Bill and Payment Suite: log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/), locate the Student Account Info card, click the Bill & Payment Suite link, choose My Account > Statements > 1098-T Tax Statements, then click View for the appropriate tax year. The PDF can be printed or saved. Forms are not mailed. [1]

For a paper copy, complete the [Revocation of Electronic 1098T form](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/wp-content/uploads/sites/147/2026/02/Revocation-of-Electronic-1098T_2026.pdf) and submit it to the Office of Student Accounts. It must be filed annually for each year you want paper; the office prints it within 5–7 business days and mails it to the home address on file with the Registrar’s Office. [1][3]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Orientation Programs says all students parking on campus need a current, valid permit. Apply online at the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/): select Permit Type and click “Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person,” then “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue”; review your request and click “Continue”; then print or save the Registration Filed page as application verification. That page is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status and “student,” not “faculty/staff.” Commuters get a rearview-mirror hang tag and may register two vehicles on one permit at no additional fee; each vehicle must be registered with Public Safety. Fees are charged to your student account. [1]

Public Safety says new students pick up permits at New Student Check-In. Returning commuter students pick up at the Public Safety ID Office Monday–Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request a different pickup time. Only one registered vehicle may be parked on campus at a time. [1][4]

Commuters may park in B1, B2, and B3. If your assigned lot is full, all students may use C1, C2, or D as overflow. Commuters may not leave a vehicle parked overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [8]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what is the deadline to drop a class without a W and how do i do it

body.answer:
I can't send messages or make changes for you, like registering, dropping a class or making a payment.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, August 28, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Tuesday, September 1, 2026: Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: Last Day to Add/Drop Winter Classes with 100% Tuition Refund (also on the Winter 2027 calendar)

Dropping in Web Self Service through and including the last day of Add/Drop means the course will not appear on your transcript [3]. The Fall 2026 dates already listed have passed [21]. If you mean another term or class session, its date depends on that term’s Academic Calendar [3].

To drop it yourself during Add/Drop, use Web Self Service [2][3]. The Registrar’s “Dropping a Course” instructions are here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/06/Dropping-a-Course.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/06/Dropping-a-Course.pdf) [3]. During the 50% refund period, you can submit the online drop form to the Office of the Registrar; the course will not appear on your transcript [5].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/online-course-information/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. Each registered guest may stay on campus no more than three nights (consecutively or not) within a seven-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. Residents may host up to two guests at a time. Roommates are automatically assumed to permit guests in shared housing, but you can contact your Resident Assistant to opt out and facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. If someone violates the contract, staff in the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before they can act. The policy recommends talking openly with your roommate about guest expectations. [3]

Contact your Resident Assistant first; for a formal complaint, contact staff in your hall/area office. Housing & Residence Life says overnight guests are not permitted on campus after Monday, December 14, 2026. [6]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
Public Safety says all students must apply online through the Parking Permits registration portal [1][5][6]. To apply, click the “RCNJ Parking Permits” link and follow the “Parking Permit Application Instructions”: log on, enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as verification. That page is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff” [1]. New student permits are picked up at New Student Check-In; returning resident students pick theirs up from their on-campus mailbox. Returning commuter students pick theirs up at the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pickup time [1][4][5]. Each vehicle must be registered; commuters may register two vehicles on one permit at no additional fee [1]. Parking fees are charged to the term bill, not paid when applying [5][9]. For Fall/Spring 2026-2027, the annual permit is $250.00; off-campus commuter tax charge is $16.58; resident parking supplement is $50.00 [16]. Off-campus students are subject to 7% sales tax, while on-campus students are exempt [5]. Student Accounts’ page lists a 6.63% rate, but Public Safety’s newer page (updated August 2026) says 7% [5][9].

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/costinfo/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

It depends on the course session: the full-semester and Session I withdrawal deadlines have passed; the Session II deadline has not. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [21][6]

After the refund period, a processed course withdrawal is recorded as a “W” on your transcript, and there is no refund. Instructor permission is not required. [6] You can withdraw online through Web Self Service (see the [instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/03/Withdrawing.pdf)), or use a withdrawal form. If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email with your name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. After withdrawing from all courses, complete the WD/LOA process in Connect. [6]

If extraordinary circumstances beyond your control prevented you from withdrawing on time, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words with official documentation to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following Fall 2026. Explain the circumstances, why you could not follow the usual process or obtain an incomplete, and which term you seek to withdraw from. A granted appeal typically results in W grades for all courses in that term. [7]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats my current balance and do i have any holds on my account

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t verify your personal balance or whether your account currently has holds. Your eBill is a statement at a point in time; later payments or charges can change what you owe. From the eBill page, click “activity since your last statement” to see activity since the bill was produced. [4]

Student Accounts says a student with an unpaid outstanding balance will have a Hold Flag, which prevents future registration, changes to existing registration, entrance into housing, and receipt of a diploma. The flag is removed once the account is paid in full, but another office may have placed a hold too. [3] Contact Student Accounts to confirm your current balance and holds.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
Candles are prohibited, and violations may lead to Student Conduct action [14]. If the allegation is activating a fire alarm by using a candle, the listed sanction is a $150 fine and fire-safety reflection for a first offense; a second offense is a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges [2]. Those are listed sanctions, not a determination of what will happen in your case.

The pages say a meeting with a Hearing Officer/College Disciplinary Review Board is an opportunity to discuss what happened [7], but don’t say whether you personally must attend one. I don’t have verified information about your case’s status or hearing requirement. Contact the Office of Student Conduct to confirm. If you have a hearing, you may submit documents or statements beforehand and may bring an advisor who cannot speak during the hearing [1]. The office can arrange an appointment to review or request the file [1].

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/frequently-asked-questions/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says that, unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at the Office. Title IV aid overpayments with a credit balance of $1.00 or greater are refunded; non-Title IV aid has a $5.00 threshold. [1]

You can instead use free electronic/direct deposit to a checking or savings account. To sign up, follow these steps: [1]
1. “Log into RCNJ Experience” [3]
2. “Locate the Student Account Info card” [3]
3. “Click on Bill & Payment Suite” [3]
4. “Click on Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu” [3]
5. “You must enroll in a Two-Step Verification Process (If previously completed, skip this step)” [3]
6. “Click on the Security Settings tab in My Profile” [3]
7. “Select a method to receive a passcode (text message, email or Google Authentication)” [3]
8. “Click the Send Code button” [3]
9. “Enter the passcode and click the Verify button” [3]
10. “Click on the Payment Profile tab in My Profile” [3]
11. “Edit existing saved Payment Method or Create New Payment Method” [3]
12. In the payment method, “click on check box in the Refund Option section to designate this payment method as the refund account for direct deposit.” [3]

After signing up, the page says to expect the refund within one to two weeks of submitting the application, if eligible. [2] For questions, contact Student Accounts.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

body.answer:
**Email:** Go to [password.ramapo.edu](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” You are eligible to set it up within 24 hours of receiving your Ramapo ID number. A valid Ramapo email account is required to register for classes. If you forget your username or password, contact Ramapo ITS. [8]
MFA is required for Ramapo Gmail. On a new device, verify your identity via the Gmail app; tap to approve the login. Trust only devices you own, never public or shared computers. **Wi-Fi:** You need a valid Ramapo email account and a wireless- or wired-capable device. Register your connection using the device you want to use before it can access the college network; once registered with ResNET, it can be used campus-wide. [14][15]
For an iPad, open Settings > Wi-Fi, select Ramapo-Secure, enter your Ramapo username and password when prompted, then click Accept on the certificate warning. [10]
For help, contact the IT Help Desk about email and ResNET about Wi-Fi.

Residence Life may reassign students for unresolved conflict and may authorize or deny room or roommate changes. [4]

question: Missed 3 classes last week because I was in the hospital. How do I get my professors to excuse the absences, is there an office that sends a note or something?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Course attendance is determined by your instructor. Speak with your instructors to determine if you can connect remotely and how to make up missed work. question: refund

body.answer:
For a credit balance, a Title IV financial aid overpayment of $1.00 or greater results in a refund; non-Title IV financial aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks cannot be sent to campus mailboxes or picked up at Student Accounts. [1]

You may request that a fall-term refund be applied to the spring term by emailing studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Spring refund proceeds cannot be applied to the following fall term. [1]

To receive a refund by free direct deposit, sign up at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/). [1] Setup steps: [6]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [12] For a late administrative withdrawal, the Office of the Provost says extraordinary circumstances may qualify, including personal illness, death of a family member, caring for a terminally ill family member, catastrophic circumstances or natural disaster, or immediate employer-required relocation. If reasons beyond your control prevented standard withdrawal or you were not granted incompletes, submit an appeal letter in your own words with official documentation to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular fall or spring semester following the term. Explain the circumstances, why standard procedures or incompletes were unavailable, and the term sought. [13] Typically, an approved appeal withdraws you from all courses in one term with W grades; exceptions may be considered. [13]

The Office of Financial Aid says officially withdrawing or leaving before 60% of a semester concludes is subject to federal rules determining how much Title IV aid may be retained or returned; meet with Financial Aid to discuss your aid package. [1] If you withdraw below full-time after the refund period, federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when fully disbursed. [24]

A course withdrawal may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress. [8] For aid SAP, students are reviewed annually after spring: the quantitative standard is completing at least 67% of attempted credits; undergraduates need a 2.0 cumulative GPA and graduate students a 3.0, and eligibility also has a 150% maximum time frame. [2] The pages do not say whether an individual W counts against these standards or determine your personal aid/SAP outcome; consult Financial Aid about your situation. [1][24]

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Orientation Programs’ page says all students parking on campus need a current, valid permit. Apply online at the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) and follow its Parking Permit Application Instructions: log on; enter Permit Type and click “Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person,” then “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue”; review the request and click “Continue”; print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as verification. That page is not your permit. Select “student” (not “faculty/staff”) and the correct commuter status. Commuters receive a rearview mirror hang tag for two registered vehicles at no extra fee; each vehicle must be registered. The fee is charged to your student account. New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning commuters pick up at the Public Safety ID Office Monday–Friday during normal operating hours, or after 3 pm at the Public Safety Main Desk if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another time. [1]

Public Safety says to ensure the parking fee is applied to your student account and visit the Parking Permits webpage. Only one of your registered vehicles may be parked on campus at a time. [4] Commuters may park in B1, B2, or B3. If your assigned lot is full, students may use C1, C2, or D as overflow. Commuters may not leave a vehicle overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [8]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. A registered guest may stay no more than three nights (consecutively or not) within a seven-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. Current residential students do not need guest registration. Residents are presumed to allow guests in shared housing, but you may opt out by contacting your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate contract. If its terms are violated, hall/area office staff need a formal complaint before acting; all residents of the space may lose guest privileges until a contract is developed. The policy recommends an open conversation about guest expectations. [3]
The last night residents may host overnight guests is Monday, December 14, 2026; none are permitted on campus after that date. Residents with an approved check-out extension may not have guests. [6]
Talk to your Resident Assistant; for a formal complaint, contact Housing & Residence Life. [3][16]

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
Orientation Programs’ FAQ says all students parking on campus must display a current, valid permit. Apply online at the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) and follow its “Parking Permit Application Instructions”: log on; enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number. That page verifies your application; it is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [1]
Commuters may register two vehicles on one hang tag at no additional fee, but each vehicle must be registered with Public Safety. The parking fee is charged to your student account. [1] New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning residents at their on-campus mailbox; returning commuters at the Public Safety ID Office during weekday normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pickup time. [1][4]
 The fee schedule also lists a $16.58 Fall/Spring Commuter Parking Tax Charge, a $50 Resident Parking Supplement, a $125 Spring-only permit for new students, and a $100 Summer-only permit. [16] The newer Public Safety page says off-campus students are charged 7% sales tax and on-campus students are exempt. [5] Older Student Accounts pages (updated June 2026 and July 2026) give a different rate, 6.63%, and list the $16.58 commuter charge. [9][16]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

Whether it’s too late depends on the course session; use the deadlines already listed above [21]. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline [6]. Before the deadline, withdrawing records a W on your transcript, with no refund; instructor permission is not required [6].

Registrar: withdraw online through Web Self Service (instructions: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/03/Withdrawing.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/03/Withdrawing.pdf)), or use the Withdrawal Form online or at the Registrar’s Office [1][6]. If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo account with your first and last name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title [6]. If withdrawing from all courses, complete the WD/LOA process in Connect using the instructions: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2022/05/LOA-WD-Instructions-10.21.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2022/05/LOA-WD-Instructions-10.21.pdf) [6]. Withdrawal may affect financial aid eligibility, progress toward graduation, athletic compliance, housing, or campus activities [1].

For extraordinary circumstances beyond your control that prevented a standard withdrawal, contact the Office of the Provost about a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words with official documentation by the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the circumstances, why standard withdrawal or an incomplete was not possible, and the term you want withdrawn. Typically, an approved appeal results in W grades in all courses for that term [7].

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

**Facilities Management**

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Offices: P-FAC [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Offices: C-102 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Get an immediate response to imminent danger: 1. If a student or the community is in imminent danger, contact Public Safety at \(201\) 684-6666. \(page: “If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

Get immediate help with an emergency when the hall/area office is closed: 1. Call Public Safety at 201-684-6666 for immediate emergency assistance when the office is closed. \(page: “If the office is closed and you need immediate assistance for an emergency, you may call Public Safety at 201-684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/facilities-services/)

This office can help:
**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

If a sexual assault took place within the past 5 days the responding officer will activate the Bergen County Sexual Assault Response Team (SART). SART is a free, coordinated community response to assist a survivor in the aftermath of a recent sexual assault. It has been designed to offer a compassionate, victim-centered approach while collecting evidence that can be vital to the investigation and prosecution of the crime. SART is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week There are three members of the SART team available to a survivor. A survivor has the option to speak with all three SART members, any combination of SART members, or speak with none of the SART members. SART members include: Forensic Nurse Examiner (FNE): A FNE is specially trained in forensic evidence collection. The FNE conducts a head to toe exam and collects evidence to assist in the prosecution of the crime. Medications to prevent Sexually Transmitted Infections and pregnancy resulting from the sexual assault are also offered to the survivor. The FNE does not treat injury; anyone needing medical attention will be seen by the attending physician in the local Emergency Department. question: whats my current balance and do i have any holds on my account

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t verify your personal balance or holds from these pages. [24][3]

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

I don’t have verified information on what will happen in your individual case or whether you must attend a hearing. Contact the Office of Student Conduct to confirm. question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says direct deposit is optional: unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check, mailed to your billing/permanent address. Checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. Title IV aid overpayments of $1.00 or greater result in a refund; non-Title IV aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. [1]

To choose free direct deposit, use the [Electronic Refunds sign-up page](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/): log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/), open the Student Account Info card, select Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds. Complete Two-Step Verification if needed, open Payment Profile, and edit or create a payment method; check the box in Refund Option to designate it for direct deposit. [3] The page says to expect your refund within one to two weeks after submitting the application, if eligible. [2] For assistance, visit Student Accounts, first floor, D-Wing. [2]

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life handles room-change requests. Visit the Room Change Process page for step-by-step details and check the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar to understand how a change might affect you. Submit a Room Change Request Form during an open room-change period; the digital form is available during active periods. Room changes are not guaranteed and depend on available space and other factors; professional Residence Life staff make the final decision. [1][2] The Office of Residence Life may reassign students for unresolved conflict, but it also reserves the right to authorize or deny room and roommate changes. [4]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts: For Spring 2027, the four- and five-month plans begin November 16, 2026. Enroll online by logging into RCNJ Experience before the semester’s posted payment deadline. The five-month plan requires a 20% down payment; the four-month plan requires 25%. Pay the down payment and the non-refundable $60 set-up fee when you enroll. Further installments are due on the 15th of each month. [1]

Past-due balances from previous semesters of $500 or more must be paid before you are eligible; the College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. Enrolling after the down-payment due date requires paying missed installments at enrollment. question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

**After the deadline:** You may not withdraw from a course after the published deadline. [12] In extraordinary circumstances that prevented completion, if you could not withdraw through standard procedures for reasons beyond your control or were not granted incompletes, you may seek a late administrative withdrawal. [13] By the last day of classes of the regular fall or spring semester following the term, submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Office of the Provost. Explain the circumstances, why standard withdrawal or incompletes were not possible, and the term you want withdrawn; if applying after the semester, explain why you did not apply earlier. [13] Typically, an approved appeal results in W grades for all courses in one term. [13]

**Aid and SAP:** Withdrawing may affect financial aid and progress toward graduation. [8] If you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits, federal aid should not be affected; NJ state aid requires full-time enrollment when it is fully disbursed. Financial Aid recommends discussing your situation with them. [23] SAP is reviewed annually after spring; students must complete at least 67% of credits attempted, and meet the GPA standard (undergraduates 2.0; graduates 3.0). [2] The pages do not specify whether a W counts as attempted or completed for SAP; ask Financial Aid. [2]

For a standard course withdrawal or help with the late-withdrawal process, contact the Registrar and Office of the Provost; contact Financial Aid about aid and SAP.

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [34]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [34]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. Each registered guest may stay on campus no more than three (3) nights (consecutively or not) within a seven (7) day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. Residents may host up to two (2) guests at a time. Current RCNJ residential students do not need to be registered as guests. The policy recommends discussing guest expectations with your roommate. [3]

Public Safety requires a current, valid permit for campus parking. Apply online through the [Parking Permits portal](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [1][5]. That page verifies your application; it is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [1] Ensure the parking fee has been applied to your student account. [4] New students pick up permits during New Student Check-In; returning resident students use their on-campus mailbox; returning commuter students pick up at the Public Safety ID Office during normal weekday hours, or after 3 pm at the Public Safety Office Main Desk if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pickup time. question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

A course withdrawal is recorded as a “W” on your transcript; there is no refund, and instructor permission is not required. The Registrar encourages discussing withdrawal with your professor. [6]

To withdraw, use Web Self Service and follow the [Withdrawing from a Course instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/03/Withdrawing.pdf). If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email the Registrar from your Ramapo account with your first and last name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. [6] You cannot withdraw after the published deadline. [6]

If circumstances beyond your control prevented a timely withdrawal, you may seek a late administrative withdrawal for extraordinary circumstances. Submit the Office of the Provost an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the extraordinary circumstances, why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or obtain an incomplete, and the term you want withdrawn. A granted appeal typically results in W grades for all courses in that term. [7]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
