question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

**Facilities Management**

Email: not listed on its pages [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/). The Facilities Management pages publish no shared unit mailbox. The General Unit Contact block gives only Service Desk and Receiving / Storeroom phone numbers, work requests go through the Service Request Portal or the Service Desk phone, and the only addresses are eight named staff members' own \(excluded\).

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Offices: P-FAC [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Offices: C-102 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

Get immediate help with an emergency when the hall/area office is closed: 1. Call Public Safety at 201-684-6666 for immediate emergency assistance when the office is closed. \(page: “If the office is closed and you need immediate assistance for an emergency, you may call Public Safety at 201-684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/facilities-services/)

This office can help:
**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Email: not listed on its pages (checked 2026-11-11) [campus-directory](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/) [campus-directory](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-request-portal/). The General Unit Contact block gives only Service Desk and Receiving / Storeroom phone numbers, work requests go through the Service Request Portal or the Service Desk phone, and the only addresses are eight named staff members' own \(excluded\).

Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
I can’t verify what will happen in your individual case. Candles are listed as prohibited; the published $150 fine and Fire Safety Reflection sanction apply to a first violation for activating a fire alarm due to disregard of a published policy, with candles as an example—not necessarily to every candle write-up. [2] The older recommended-sanctions page gives the same first-violation amount and reflection sanction. For a second violation, the newer page says $300, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges; the older page says possible suspension of residence privileges. [2][6] The older page was updated October 2022; the newer page was updated August 2025. [2][6]

The pages don’t say that every RA write-up requires a hearing or whether you personally must attend. Confirm with the Office of Student Conduct. If a hearing is scheduled, you may review the statements and incident reports the complainant will use by contacting the Office to arrange an appointment or request the file; you may have an advisor, who cannot speak during the hearing. [1]

**Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says a credit balance from Title IV aid of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; non-Title IV aid has a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up in the office. [1]

Direct deposit is free and optional. To enroll, go to [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) and follow these steps: [1][3]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)
2. Locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite.
3. Click Electronic Refunds on the right under My Profile Setup.
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in My Profile, select Security Settings, choose a method for the passcode, click Send Code, enter it, and click Verify.
5. In Payment Profile, edit a saved payment method or create a new one, then check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it for direct deposit. [3]

After applying, eligible refunds are expected within one to two weeks. [2] For help, contact Student Accounts; its page lists the office location as first floor, D-Wing. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts: To add your parent, follow the [Authorized User setup instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/users/):
1. “Log into RCNJ Experience” and “Locate the Student Account Info card.”
2. “Click on Bill & Payment Suite link,” then “Click on Authorized Users” in the My Profile Setup section.
3. “Click on the Add Authorized User tab.” Enter your parent’s email, answer the questions, and click Continue. Click the “I Agree” box, then Continue. [4]

This lets your parent make payments. If you want them to pay without seeing your bill or payment history, select “No” for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” [1][3] Authorized Users can make payments through the Bill & Payment Suite. [5]

Being an Authorized User does not allow Student Accounts to discuss your financial records with your parent. If you want that permission, the newer FAQ directs you to the [Registrar’s Office FERPA Waiver form](https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open). [1][6] The older “Allow Others to Make a Payment and/or View Your Bill” page (updated March 2026) instead refers to an Office of Student Accounts FERPA Waiver Form. [1][6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

question: how do i set up my campus email and wifi login

body.answer:
**Email — Registrar:** New students can set up their Ramapo email within 24 hours of receiving their Ramapo ID number. Visit [password.ramapo.edu](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” A valid Ramapo email account is required to register for classes. If you forget your username or password, contact Ramapo ITS. [8] The page also links to the [New Student Account Setup Workflow](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/wp-content/uploads/sites/102/2026/02/NewAccountWorkflow2.png). [1]

**Email sign-in — IT Help Desk:** MFA is required for Ramapo Gmail. On a new device, verify your identity through the Gmail app on your phone; tap to approve. You can select “Trust this device” on a personal device, but never trust a public or shared computer. The setup process is the same on PC, Mac, iPhone, and Android. [2][4] See the [step-by-step 2FA instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mfa). [4]

**Wi-Fi — ResNET:** Register your device before it can connect to the college network. On the [registration page](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/), select the wired or wireless registration link. [14] To connect wirelessly, scan for networks and connect; see the [Wireless page](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/secure-wireless/). [17]

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life handles room changes; room and board changes must go through its office. [7]
1. Review the [Room Change Process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) and the [Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/) to understand how a change might affect you. [1]
2. Submit the Room Change Request Form during the open room change period. The [online form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog) is available during active room change periods. [2, 5]
Room changes are not guaranteed; decisions depend on available space and other factors, and final decisions are made by professional Residence Life staff. The office may reassign a student for unresolved conflict, but that does not guarantee a requested change. [1, 4]
If approved, prorated housing charges and any applicable meal-plan changes will be assessed and adjusted on your student account. [2]

- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]
- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Missed 3 classes last week because I was in the hospital. How do I get my professors to excuse the absences, is there an office that sends a note or something?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

If your hospitalization was related to a medical disability, the Office of Specialized Services says to contact each faculty member after an absence to account for it and determine if and when work may be made up. The instructor sets the attendance policy; OSS can consult with students and faculty about what is appropriate. [10] I don’t have verified information that an office sends professors an excuse note for a hospitalization.

question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

body.answer:

Alumni can use the library’s online services, borrow books and access the Learning Commons. question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says all on-campus positions are posted on Handshake. Register at [https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/](https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/) to view openings, search using the keyword “RCNJ,” and follow the application instructions on each posting; contact the listed supervisor. Students awarded Federal Work-Study receive priority for Student Assistant positions. [5]

Apply directly to the hiring unit. If offered a position and you accept, you and the supervisor sign an employment form. Return all required paperwork—the New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form—to the Student Assistant Program Office in Room D-119. [1]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [21]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts: Spring 2027 four- and five-month plans are available beginning November 16, 2026. Enroll online by logging into RCNJ Experience ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)) before the posted semester payment deadline. The four-month plan has a 25% down payment; the five-month plan has a 20% down payment. The down payment and fee are due when you enroll; later installments are due on the 15th of each month. The four-month plan’s installments are due January, February, March and April. [1][3]
There is a non-refundable $60 set-up fee for Spring 2027. [1] A $500 or greater past-due balance from a previous semester must be paid before you’re eligible; the College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. Missing the payment deadline may result in a $200 late fee and/or deregistration. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/affordability/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
For the 2027–2028 FAFSA, returning students should apply by April 1; new students by May 1. [14] An older Financial Aid “Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)” page, updated July 2025, gives March 15 for new students. [12]

To be considered for aid, you must be accepted to Ramapo and complete a FAFSA; provide your Social Security number on your admissions application. [29] Use Ramapo School Code 009344. [31] To see what additional documents are specifically required of you, visit RCNJ Experience, log into MyRamapo with your Ramapo username and password, select the Financial Aid Self-Service box, choose Financial Aid Dashboard, and select 26-27 Aid Year in the upper-right Aid Year dropdown if it is not already displayed. [30]

NJ residents seeking state aid: on the 2026–2027 FAFSA confirmation page, select the “optional feature” link to apply for NJ State based Financial Aid. If you did not, go to www.hesaa.org 3-5 business days after submitting the FAFSA, select “Report Additional Information for State Aid,” and create a login to provide the requested information online. [24]

- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [33]
- **Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [33]

Sources: [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/fafsa/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/admissions/financial-aid-tuition/financial-aid-deadlines/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/new-students/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/financial-aid-forms/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/new-students/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [12] If you have extraordinary circumstances that prevented you from completing the semester and reasons beyond your control kept you from using standard procedures (or you were not granted incompletes), you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal through the Office of the Provost. Examples include personal illness; death of a family member, spouse, or partner; caring for a terminally ill family member, spouse, or partner; recovery from catastrophic circumstances or natural disaster; or immediate relocation required by an employer. [13]

Submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular (fall or spring) semester following the term you want withdrawn. Explain the extraordinary circumstances, why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or obtain incompletes, and—if applying after the end of that semester—why you did not apply sooner; indicate the term. [13] A granted appeal typically results in W grades for all courses in one term; exceptions may be made in extraordinary circumstances. [13]

Withdrawing may affect financial aid eligibility and progress toward graduation. [8] Financial Aid reviews aid SAP annually after spring: students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits and meet the applicable GPA standard (undergraduates 2.0; graduates 3.0). [2] Its aid guidance says dropping below full-time can adjust aid: for example, going from 12 to 6 credits reduces federal Pell but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled and institutional grants or scholarships reduced or taken away. [3] Academic scholarships or Ramapo grants may also be reduced or taken away below 12 credits. [5]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
Orientation Programs’ instructions: apply online at the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). Log on, enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information, then Continue; review your request, then Continue. Print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as verification; it is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status. Fees are charged to your student account. Commuters may register two vehicles on one permit at no extra fee, but each must be registered and only one may be parked on campus at a time. [1][4] Permits for new students are available for pickup during New Student Check-In. [1][4]

Public Safety authorizes commuters to park in B1, B2, and B3. If your assigned lot is full, students may use C1, C2, or D as overflow. Commuters may not leave a vehicle overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [8]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

question: I'm a commuter student and I have a 3 hour gap between classes. Is there somewhere on campus I can study or hang out, like a commuter lounge, and is there a way to store my stuff?

body.answer:
The Center for Student Involvement describes J. Lee’s as the unofficial Commuter Lounge, for relaxing before or after class. It’s on the second floor of the Student Center, between the Student Government office and the Black Student Union office; it has video games, pool, ping pong and free popcorn. [1] The Center also describes J. Lee’s as a spot to hang out between classes, next to the Black Student Union and Student Government Association offices. [2]

The Women’s Center & LGBTQ+ Services welcomes students to its Room C-220 lounge during open hours to hang out, socialize or study; it has comfortable seating, a coffee maker, refrigerator and microwave. [14] The Birch Tree Inn describes the Student Center Atrium as having ample lounging areas. [20]

The Center for Student Involvement says students may rent small or medium lockers for the academic semesters at the Student Center Office. Lockers are in the second-floor stairwell area between B and C buildings. The fee is $10.00 for the semester or $20.00 for the academic year. A key is issued with payment and must be returned at the end of the semester. [6]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [21]

question: what is the deadline to drop a class without a W and how do i do it

body.answer:
I can't send messages or make changes for you, like registering, dropping a class or making a payment.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, August 28, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Tuesday, September 1, 2026: Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: Last Day to Add/Drop Winter Classes with 100% Tuition Refund (also on the Winter 2027 calendar)

To drop without the course appearing on your transcript, drop it online in Web Self Service by the last day of Add/Drop. During the 50% refund period, use the online drop form and submit it to the Registrar by the date on the Academic Calendar; the catalog says the dropped course will not appear on your transcript. [3][5] The Fall 2026 dates already listed above are 100% add/drop deadlines; the information here does not give a 50% drop deadline. Check the Academic Calendar for your term’s deadline. [3][5]

The Registrar’s “Dropping a Course” page links to the [Dropping-a-Course instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/06/Dropping-a-Course.pdf). [3]

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. Each registered guest may stay on campus no more than three (3) nights (consecutively or not) within a seven (7) day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. The policy permits up to two guests at a time. Residents are responsible for guests, and roommates are responsible for telling the host about concerns. The College assumes roommates agree to guests unless you opt out by contacting your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. If a contract is violated, hall/area office staff need a formal complaint before they can act. A complaint may mean all residents lose guest privileges until they develop a contract. The page recommends an open conversation about guest expectations. [3]
Talk to your Resident Assistant about opting out/setting up a contract; if the contract is violated, submit a formal complaint to hall/area office staff. Housing & Residence Life is the relevant office. [3]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
Orientation Programs’ FAQ says all students must apply online through the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) and follow its Parking Permit Application Instructions. [1] To apply: log on to the site; enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as verification. That page is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [1] Each vehicle must be registered. [1]

New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning residents at their on-campus mailbox; returning commuters at the Public Safety ID Office Monday–Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request a different pickup time. [4] The parking fee is charged to your term bill, not paid when applying. [5]

For 2026–2027, the annual Fall/Spring permit is $250; the listed commuter tax charge is $16.58, and the resident parking supplement is $50. [16] Public Safety says off-campus students are subject to 7% sales tax and on-campus students are exempt. [5] An older Student Accounts page, updated June 2026, says the tax is 6.63%. [9]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

For a Session I or full-semester course, the listed withdrawal deadline has passed; for a Session II course, it has not [21]. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline [6].

The Registrar says that after the refund period, a course withdrawal is recorded as a “W” on your transcript, with no refund; instructor permission is not required, though discussing it with your professor is encouraged [6]. To withdraw before the deadline, use Web Self Service and its instructions: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/03/Withdrawing.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/03/Withdrawing.pdf) [6]. If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email with your first and last name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title [6].

If extraordinary circumstances beyond your control kept you from withdrawing on time, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, with official documentation, to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular semester following the term. Explain the circumstances, why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or obtain incompletes, and the term you want withdrawn [7]. Typically, approval means W grades in all courses for that term [7].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

value.page_words: REPORTING TO THE MAHWAH POLICE DEPARTMENT: The Mahwah Police Department (http://www.mahwahpd.org/)can be reached by calling (201) 529-1000 or by calling 911. If a sexual assault took place within the past 5 days the responding officer will activate the Bergen County Sexual Assault Response Team (SART). SART is a free, coordinated community response to assist a survivor in the aftermath of a recent sexual assault. It has been designed to offer a compassionate, victim-centered approach while collecting evidence that can be vital to the investigation and prosecution of the crime. SART is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week There are three members of the SART team available to a survivor. A survivor has the option to speak with all three SART members, any combination of SART members, or speak with none of the SART members. SART members include: Forensic Nurse Examiner (FNE): A FNE is specially trained in forensic evidence collection. The FNE conducts a head to toe exam and collects evidence to assist in the prosecution of the crime. Medications to prevent Sexually Transmitted Infections and pregnancy resulting from the sexual assault are also offered to the survivor. The FNE does not treat injury; anyone needing medical attention will be seen by the attending physician in the local Emergency Department. question: whats my current balance and do i have any holds on my account

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I don’t have verified information about your personal balance or whether your account has holds. To check your bill, go to Web Self Service: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/?name=homepage&accessibility=true) [30]. Your eBill is a statement at a point in time; click “activity since your last statement” to see activity since it was generated [4]. In the Bill & Payment Suite, the Account Summary screen shows pending financial aid in separate sections; “Current Due Net of Authorized Financial Aid and Memos” is the amount to be paid [6].

The Office of Student Accounts is the primary manager of student accounts [23]. Any student with an outstanding unpaid balance will have a Hold Flag; paying the account in full removes that flag, but another office or department may have a separate hold [3]. For help with a financial hold, contact Student Accounts [15]. The Center for Student Success says a Junior advisement hold this semester requires scheduling a meeting with your faculty academic advisor; after the meeting, they will lift the hold so you can register for Summer and Fall [16].

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [33]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
Candles are prohibited in residence halls, and students who violate fire-safety rules may face disciplinary action [14]. The pages don’t say what happens after a particular RA write-up or whether your case requires a hearing. Contact the Office of Student Conduct to ask about your case [1].

If a candle caused a fire-alarm activation due to disregard of a published policy, the Fire Safety page lists a first offense as a $150.00 fine and fire-safety reflection assignment, and a second as a $300.00 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges [2]. This sanction is for that alarm-activation violation; the pages don’t give a specific sanction for candle possession alone. The older “Recommended Judicial Sanctions” page, updated October 2022, gives different wording for the second offense [6].

If you have a hearing, you may review the written statements and incident reports the complainant will use; contact the Office of Student Conduct to arrange an appointment or request the file. You may have an advisor of your choosing attend, but the advisor cannot speak during the hearing [1].

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/recommended-judicial-sanctions/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says a Title IV aid overpayment that leaves a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; non-Title IV aid credit balances are subject to a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. [1]

Direct deposit is optional and free. To use it, sign up at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/). [1][2] The steps are: [4]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/).
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click Bill & Payment Suite.
3. Click Electronic Refunds on the right under My Profile Setup.
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in My Profile, open Security Settings, select a passcode method (text, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify.
5. Open Payment Profile. Edit a saved payment method or create one, then check the box in Refund Option to designate it for direct deposit.

After applying, expect an eligible refund to be deposited within one to two weeks. With direct deposit, a check isn’t printed or mailed. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts: Follow the setup instructions at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/users/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/users/) [4]: “Log into RCNJ Experience” → “Locate the Student Account Info card” → “Click on Bill & Payment Suite link” → “Click on Authorized Users located on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section” → “Click on the Add Authorized User tab” → “Enter the email address of the desired authorized user, answer questions, and click the Continue button” → “Click I Agree box then the Continue button.” [4] Authorized Users can make payments on your behalf. [1] If you want your parent to make payments without seeing your bill or payment history, select “No” for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” [3] The Bill & Payment Suite is where Authorized Users can make payments. [5]

Adding an Authorized User does not give Student Accounts permission to discuss your financial records with them. To allow that, complete and submit the Registrar’s Office FERPA Waiver form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open](https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open). [1][6] An older Student Accounts page, updated March 2026, says “Office of Student Accounts FERPA Waiver Form.” [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/users/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/users/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i set up my campus email and wifi login

body.answer:
Registrar: New students can set up a Ramapo email account within 24 hours of receiving their Ramapo ID number. Visit [https://password.ramapo.edu/](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” A valid Ramapo email account is required to register for classes. [8]

Ramapo Gmail requires MFA. When you sign in on a new device, approve the prompt in the Gmail app on your phone. You can choose “Trust this device” on a personal device; do not trust public or shared computers. [4][2]

ResNET: You need a valid Ramapo email account and a wireless- or wired-network-capable device. Register the device you’ll use with ResNET before connecting; once registered, it can be used campus-wide. [6][3] Go to [https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/), choose wired or wireless ([https://resnet.ramapo.edu/register/login.php](https://resnet.ramapo.edu/register/login.php) or [http://mydevices.ramapo.edu/](http://mydevices.ramapo.edu/)), and retrieve the MAC address for the connection you’ll use: [https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/). [14][15] Then scan for wireless networks and connect; see [https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/secure-wireless/](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/secure-wireless/) for wireless instructions. [17]

For setup help, contact the IT Help Desk about email or ResNET about Wi-Fi. [8][17]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [21]
- **IT Help Desk**: Phone: (201) 684-7777. Email: helpdesk@ramapo.edu. Location: 4th floor of the Learning Commons. [21]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/mfa/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/faqs/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/email-activation-and-information/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/its/faqs/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/online-course-information/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/register/) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life: Submit a Room Change Request Form during the open room change period; it is available during active room change periods. Review the full process and check the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar to understand how a room change might affect you. Room changes are not guaranteed; they depend on available space and other factors, and final decisions are made by professional Residence Life staff. [1][2]

Use the [Room Change Process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) page for step-by-step details and the [Online Room Change Request Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog). [1][5] Residence Life reserves the right to reassign students for unresolved conflict. [4] Room and board changes must be done through the Office of Residence Life. [7]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

body.answer:
Yes. **Career services:** The Office of Alumni Relations says alumni can use the Cahill Career Center’s services on campus, including help with job searches, resume updates, interviewing skills and more. For additional information, contact the Cahill Career Center at (201) 684-7444 or careercenter@ramapo.edu. [2] The college also says career guidance and resume help are alumni benefits, and access to career counseling extends to all Ramapo alumni. [6][8]

**Library:** Alumni can use the library’s online services, borrow books, and access the Learning Commons. Visit the [library website](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/) for more information, or download the [Library Benefits document](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/wp-content/uploads/sites/195/2013/08/Library-Benefits.doc). [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/benefits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/benefits/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/commencement/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/)

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says all federal work-study positions are posted on Handshake; register there, search open positions (use keyword “RCNJ”), and apply directly to the hiring unit by following the individual posting’s instructions. Contact the listed supervisor. [1][5] If offered a position and you accept, you and the supervisor sign an employment form; return the required New Hire Packet, W-4 Form, and I-9 Form to the Student Assistant Program Office, Room D-119. [1]

Since you’ve been awarded Federal Work-Study, you have priority for Student Assistant positions. For questions about your award, contact Financial Aid at finaid@ramapo.edu. [5]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/policies-and-procedures/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
